question: At 9 weeks of pregnancy, which ultrasound measurement provides the most accurate estimation of gestational age?

answers.text: Biparietal diameter (BPD), because the skull is well-formed by the first trimester

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: BPD is used in the second trimester (16–20 weeks). In the first trimester, the skull is not adequately ossified for reliable BPD measurement.

answers.text: Crown-rump length (CRL), the gold standard for first-trimester dating

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! CRL measured between 7 and 13+6 weeks is the most accurate single measurement for gestational age, with an accuracy of ±5–7 days. It is the gold standard for first-trimester dating.

answers.text: Femur length (FL), because the long bones grow at a constant rate early in pregnancy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Femur length is used for second- and third-trimester dating and has higher biological variability. It is not the preferred first-trimester measurement.

answers.text: Abdominal circumference (AC), which reflects fetal nutrition most accurately

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: AC is primarily used for growth assessment in the second and third trimester. In the first trimester, the abdomen is too small for reliable circumference measurement.

overallFeedback.feedback: Crown-rump length (CRL) at 7–13+6 weeks is the gold standard for first-trimester gestational age dating, accurate to ±5–7 days.
Excellent! CRL between 7 and 13+6 weeks is the most accurate gestational age measurement, ±5–7 days.
